title: NHS6 - Weekly Enclosure Coordination
summary_text:
Introductions: New Sphere Team Members
Jeff Hamman leading the Sphere Maryland project
Rebeca Golden on design side
Larry Golden, VP of Construction Onsite (joining calls this week, catching up)
Joe LaPara, project manager from D&C, joining from studios and the original Las Vegas Sphere build
Extensive background in LED interior and exterior systems
Katie Abek, project manager (not on call), will be on site
Guido Perego, project manager for technology division, working with Tom and Darren
Served as owner representative for audio on the Las Vegas project
Exterior Enclosure Systems: Evaluation Matrix
Buro Happold tasked with broad evaluation of exterior systems against Sphere Maryland wish list
Key criteria: dark/matte finish, acoustic performance, modularity
Three systems under evaluation: insulated precast concrete, cold-formed metal frame panel, unitized curtain wall mega-panel
Matrix document in progress: Excel tracker categorizing systems across multiple criteria buckets
Criteria include acoustics, cost, maintenance, and other factors
Next step: circulate this week for team to rank criteria by importance to the project
Sphere team asked to use RAG (red/amber/green) and good/better/best ranking format
Acoustic layer (Buro Happold) to be tied into the matrix alongside thermal/environmental criteria
Concept Plus acoustic report assumed a 6-inch concrete shell as baseline for acoustic performance
Manica architectural report envisioned precast panel with rail carrier and Sentry panel
Precast Concrete System
Key advantage: finish achievable on both interior and exterior faces; insulation contained within panel
Weight remains the heaviest option of the three systems
Jointing: two lines of sealant at both vertical and horizontal joints (belt and suspenders)
Cracking on exterior surface does not necessarily telegraph through the full panel
Pushback noted on crack control; preference expressed for rain screen as belt-and-suspenders approach
Local suppliers within roughly a 4-hour drive; numerous precast suppliers in Canada with US project history
Next step: quick conversation with structural (Sarah Root) to confirm loads held for exterior wall assembly
Cold-Formed Metal Frame Panel and Unitized Curtain Wall Systems
Cold-formed metal frame: joint condition identified as the main area for further evaluation
Relies solely on sealant joint (two lines); no gasketed system
Multiple contractors in region capable of building to finish; various finish options (metal panel, stucco, etc.)
Unitized curtain wall mega-panel: gasketed male/female connection at both vertical and horizontal joints
Does not rely solely on sealant; weather sealant applied inboard without a second-pass requirement
Likely the most expensive of the three systems
Two manufacturers flagged for curtain wall approach: Eastern (Pennsylvania) and Island Exteriors (Long Island, NY)
Buro Happold can arrange presentations with either if Sphere team wishes
Clover system recap: metal panel on steel frame, sealant joint only, no drainage cavity
Closer to a surface barrier system than a true rain screen
Capacity to add a second metal layer exists but adds depth and cost
Roof Waterproofing Strategy
Dome surface: spray polyurea proposed as primary robust waterproofing layer
Spray foam above polyurea, then finished surface
Rationale: Vegas spray foam system deemed insufficient for higher-demand Maryland conditions
Flat/conventional roof areas: cover board system with membrane (spray or cold fluid applied) plus walk pads
Hot fluid applied not recommended due to slump risk and application complexity
Transition between dome and flat: seamless if polyurethane fluid-applied system used throughout
Products under consideration: Guardian and Henry ProDeck
Reflectance requirements under IPC energy code must be addressed while avoiding bright white finish
More rooftop equipment and access expected vs. Las Vegas; long-term durability a priority
Below-Grade Waterproofing
Groundwater table is shallow: 4 to 6 feet below grade
Proposed robust system: blind-side waterproofing below slab, post-applied to walls
Components: insulation, membrane, reverse asphalt, drainage mat
Products considered: Tremco Supreme 1000, Oximate, Grace 3000
Perimeter drain and sub-slab drains (approx. every 5 feet) per geotech recommendation
Current assumption: full slab waterproofed, not just pits and trench
Team to revisit whether full-slab extent is warranted vs. a simpler system in lower-risk zones
Geotech environmental testing (soil contaminants) still in progress
Terrazzo floor finish flagged as a risk: any water migration could cause failure
Breathable or tile alternatives discussed as potentially more forgiving
Next step: Buro Happold to produce slab edge plan with one-line diagram showing 4D trench location and good/better/best waterproofing assembly recommendations by zone
Steel Coating and Additional Enclosure Topics
Structural steel coating (large steel cage wrapping the building) needs to be incorporated into the enclosure strategy
Intumescent coating previously discussed; team to confirm whether it remains the right system for a non-coastal, high-humidity Maryland climate
Cost-conscious approach: confirm whether intumescent is the minimum acceptable or the preferred system
Blast/threat mitigation: Jensen Hughes engaged; their findings may eliminate certain facade systems
Proximity threats (vehicles, backpacks) being evaluated; report pending
RWBI wind loading analysis underway; snow and ice loading to be addressed in a later phase
FM Global insurance requirements: not confirmed as applicable at this time
Team curious about cost delta if FM Global standards were applied to roof and waterproofing design
Intent is to be master label prepared and designed to standard, but not necessarily execute the label
Next Steps
Circulate exterior systems comparison matrix to Sphere team (Buro Happold)
Send this week for criteria ranking; include RAG and good/better/best scoring; tie in acoustic performance data.
Produce slab edge plan with waterproofing assembly diagram (Buro Happold)
Show 4D trench location and good/better/best assembly options by zone to right-size the below-grade system.
Confirm structural loads held for exterior wall assembly
Coordinate with Sarah Root to verify what loads are assumed for the exterior wall, given precast weight implications.
Send preliminary enclosure presentation to TVS for distribution to Sphere team (Buro Happold)
TVS to distribute; also upload to ACC separately and attach to meeting minutes.
Loop steel coating strategy into overall enclosure presentation
Confirm whether intumescent is the right system for Maryland's climate and where it sits on the good/better/best scale.

# Introductions: New Sphere Team Members

- Jeff Hamman leading the Sphere Maryland project
- Rebeca Golden on design side
- Larry Golden, VP of Construction Onsite (joining calls this week, catching up)
- Joe LaPara, project manager from D\&C, joining from studios and the original Las Vegas Sphere build
  - Extensive background in LED interior and exterior systems
- Katie Abek, project manager (not on call), will be on site
- Guido Perego, project manager for technology division, working with Tom and Darren
  - Served as owner representative for audio on the Las Vegas project

# Exterior Enclosure Systems: Evaluation Matrix

- Buro Happold tasked with broad evaluation of exterior systems against Sphere Maryland wish list
  - Key criteria: dark/matte finish, acoustic performance, modularity
- Three systems under evaluation: insulated precast concrete, cold-formed metal frame panel, unitized curtain wall mega-panel
- Matrix document in progress: Excel tracker categorizing systems across multiple criteria buckets
  - Criteria include acoustics, cost, maintenance, and other factors
  - Next step: circulate this week for team to rank criteria by importance to the project
- Sphere team asked to use RAG (red/amber/green) and good/better/best ranking format
- Acoustic layer (Buro Happold) to be tied into the matrix alongside thermal/environmental criteria
- Concept Plus acoustic report assumed a 6-inch concrete shell as baseline for acoustic performance
  - Manica architectural report envisioned precast panel with rail carrier and Sentry panel

# Precast Concrete System

- Key advantage: finish achievable on both interior and exterior faces; insulation contained within panel
- Weight remains the heaviest option of the three systems
- Jointing: two lines of sealant at both vertical and horizontal joints (belt and suspenders)
  - Cracking on exterior surface does not necessarily telegraph through the full panel
- Pushback noted on crack control; preference expressed for rain screen as belt-and-suspenders approach
- Local suppliers within roughly a 4-hour drive; numerous precast suppliers in Canada with US project history
- Next step: quick conversation with structural (Sarah Root) to confirm loads held for exterior wall assembly

# Cold-Formed Metal Frame Panel and Unitized Curtain Wall Systems

- Cold-formed metal frame: joint condition identified as the main area for further evaluation
  - Relies solely on sealant joint (two lines); no gasketed system
  - Multiple contractors in region capable of building to finish; various finish options (metal panel, stucco, etc.)
- Unitized curtain wall mega-panel: gasketed male/female connection at both vertical and horizontal joints
  - Does not rely solely on sealant; weather sealant applied inboard without a second-pass requirement
  - Likely the most expensive of the three systems
- Two manufacturers flagged for curtain wall approach: Eastern (Pennsylvania) and Island Exteriors (Long Island, NY)
  - Buro Happold can arrange presentations with either if Sphere team wishes
- Clover system recap: metal panel on steel frame, sealant joint only, no drainage cavity
  - Closer to a surface barrier system than a true rain screen
  - Capacity to add a second metal layer exists but adds depth and cost

# Roof Waterproofing Strategy

- Dome surface: spray polyurea proposed as primary robust waterproofing layer
  - Spray foam above polyurea, then finished surface
  - Rationale: Vegas spray foam system deemed insufficient for higher-demand Maryland conditions
- Flat/conventional roof areas: cover board system with membrane (spray or cold fluid applied) plus walk pads
  - Hot fluid applied not recommended due to slump risk and application complexity
- Transition between dome and flat: seamless if polyurethane fluid-applied system used throughout
- Products under consideration: Guardian and Henry ProDeck
- Reflectance requirements under IPC energy code must be addressed while avoiding bright white finish
- More rooftop equipment and access expected vs. Las Vegas; long-term durability a priority

# Below-Grade Waterproofing

- Groundwater table is shallow: 4 to 6 feet below grade
- Proposed robust system: blind-side waterproofing below slab, post-applied to walls
  - Components: insulation, membrane, reverse asphalt, drainage mat
  - Products considered: Tremco Supreme 1000, Oximate, Grace 3000
  - Perimeter drain and sub-slab drains (approx. every 5 feet) per geotech recommendation
- Current assumption: full slab waterproofed, not just pits and trench
  - Team to revisit whether full-slab extent is warranted vs. a simpler system in lower-risk zones
- Geotech environmental testing (soil contaminants) still in progress
- Terrazzo floor finish flagged as a risk: any water migration could cause failure
  - Breathable or tile alternatives discussed as potentially more forgiving
- Next step: Buro Happold to produce slab edge plan with one-line diagram showing 4D trench location and good/better/best waterproofing assembly recommendations by zone

# Steel Coating and Additional Enclosure Topics

- Structural steel coating (large steel cage wrapping the building) needs to be incorporated into the enclosure strategy
  - Intumescent coating previously discussed; team to confirm whether it remains the right system for a non-coastal, high-humidity Maryland climate
  - Cost-conscious approach: confirm whether intumescent is the minimum acceptable or the preferred system
- Blast/threat mitigation: Jensen Hughes engaged; their findings may eliminate certain facade systems
  - Proximity threats (vehicles, backpacks) being evaluated; report pending
- RWBI wind loading analysis underway; snow and ice loading to be addressed in a later phase
- FM Global insurance requirements: not confirmed as applicable at this time
  - Team curious about cost delta if FM Global standards were applied to roof and waterproofing design
  - Intent is to be master label prepared and designed to standard, but not necessarily execute the label

# Next Steps

- **Circulate exterior systems comparison matrix to Sphere team** (Buro Happold)

  Send this week for criteria ranking; include RAG and good/better/best scoring; tie in acoustic performance data.
- **Produce slab edge plan with waterproofing assembly diagram** (Buro Happold)

  Show 4D trench location and good/better/best assembly options by zone to right-size the below-grade system.
- **Confirm structural loads held for exterior wall assembly**

  Coordinate with Sarah Root to verify what loads are assumed for the exterior wall, given precast weight implications.
- **Send preliminary enclosure presentation to TVS for distribution to Sphere team** (Buro Happold)

  TVS to distribute; also upload to ACC separately and attach to meeting minutes.
- **Loop steel coating strategy into overall enclosure presentation**

  Confirm whether intumescent is the right system for Maryland's climate and where it sits on the good/better/best scale.
